item.title: One Issue That Could Upend Fragile U.S.-China Ties: Taiwan Arms
item.description: As Beijing presses President Trump to freeze a proposed $14 billion weapons sale to the island, Taiwan is trying to show that its security is in U.S. interests.
item.dc:creator: Chris Buckley and Amy Chang Chien
item.media:description: President Trump and China’s leader, Xi Jinping, in Beijing in May. Mr. Trump has held off on arms sales to Taiwan as he has sought pragmatic ties with China.

item.title: U.S. and China Discuss System to Warn of A.I. National Security Issues
item.description: In a meeting on Sunday, the U.S. Treasury secretary and China’s vice premier talked about having a shared vision on the goals of artificial intelligence and the threats it poses.
item.dc:creator: Alan Rappeport, Lauren Hirsch and Ana Swanson
item.media:description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Sunday that the alert system would be activated when a matter related to artificial intelligence reaches the national security level.

item.title: China Promised to Buy More U.S. Farm Goods. It Hasn’t Happened.
item.description: Soybeans are the notable exception, revealing Beijing’s selective approach to fulfilling trade commitments ahead of the summit between President Trump and Xi Jinping.
item.dc:creator: Sui-Lee Wee
item.media:credit: KC McGinnis for The New York Times
item.media:description: In May, China agreed to buy at least $17 billion in U.S. farm goods a year through 2028. China had already vowed separately to step up purchases of American soybeans.

item.title: Germany’s Merz Vows to Stay After Another State Election ‘Disaster’

item.media:description: “What needs to be done now requires backbone, steadfastness and patience,” Chancellor Friedrich Merz of Germany said Sunday.
